change.title: Text Completions API marked deprecated in TypeScript SDK 0.132.0 (Python v1.0 removed it)

source.quote: **api:** mark the Text Completions API as deprecated

tasks.reasoning: The source entry concerns the TypeScript SDK, but it also states that Python SDK v1.0 removed Text Completions. This repo depends on that API through the Python SDK. The pinned 0.2.10 still exposes completion, so nothing breaks just from this notice. However, any SDK upgrade past 1.0 removes the method. The models usable with Text Completions (claude-1.x, claude-2.x, claude-instant) have also already been retired on the Claude API, so this call site probably fails today whatever SDK is installed. The migration agent should: (1) check which model string is passed at line 36; (2) rewrite the call to client.messages.create with a supported current model, converting the Human/Assistant prompt into messages, max_tokens_to_sample into max_tokens and stop_sequences as-is; (3) read content[0].text instead of .completion in the response handling, which the scan did not read; (4) bump anthropic in requirements.txt to a current version. Uncertain: whether the benchmark is still run. If it is, it is likely already broken.

callSites.why: Calls the legacy Text Completions API (prompt, stop_sequences, max_tokens_to_sample) through the Python anthropic SDK pinned at ==0.2.10. Anthropic has now deprecated this API: the TypeScript SDK marks it deprecated, and Python SDK v1.0 removed client.completions entirely.

record.prBody:
## Text Completions API marked deprecated in TypeScript SDK 0.132.0 (Python v1.0 removed it) [Verified]

### Change

benchmark/kobbq/util.py get_claude_response now uses anthropic.Anthropic().messages.create instead of the removed Client.completion. The Human/Assistant prompt became a single user message, max_tokens_to_sample became max_tokens, and stop_sequences was dropped. The response is read from content text blocks instead of ["completion"]. CLAUDE_MODEL changed to claude-haiku-4-5 and claude-sonnet-4-5, because claude-instant-1.2 and claude-2.0 are retired. requirements.txt now pins anthropic==2.4.0. Added tests/test_kobbq_claude.py, which runs the real function against a mocked HTTP transport.

Files touched:
- `benchmark/kobbq/util.py`
- `requirements.txt`
- `tests/test_kobbq_claude.py`

### Why

The source says the Text Completions API is deprecated, and Python SDK v1.0 removed it. The old call would break on any SDK upgrade, and the models it used are retired.

> **api:** mark the Text Completions API as deprecated

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| kobbq-claude-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- kobbq-claude-test, added by the agent: `python -m pytest tests/test_kobbq_claude.py -q` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `anthropic__package_lookup`: pass

Test of this change: `kobbq-claude-test`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container python:3.12-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- No live call was made, so it is unconfirmed that the new model ids behave well on the KoBBQ prompts.
- Commented-out model names in kobbq.py and kobbq_demo.py still show the old claude-instant-1.2 and claude-2.0.
- The full requirements.txt install was not verified: several unrelated pins (levenshtein, BlackBoxAuditing, ecos) already failed to install in the sandbox.
- anthropic 2.x requires Python >=3.10 and sends API version 2026-10-21. Both are untested against the rest of the repo's pins.
- The new test's pre-change failure is only because the test file and the new call did not exist yet. It does not independently show the old behaviour.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Allowed Claude model names changed. Existing CLI args that pass claude-instant-1.2 or claude-2.0 now fail the assert.
- The \n\nHuman: stop sequence is no longer sent, because the Messages API has no use for it.
- The prompt is now a plain user message rather than Human/Assistant-formatted text.
- The returned string is the concatenated text blocks, with no leading-space convention from the old completions output.

review.summary: The only named call site (benchmark/kobbq/util.py:36) moves correctly from the Text Completions API (`Client.completion`, `max_tokens_to_sample`, `resp["completion"]`) to `anthropic.Anthropic().messages.create` and reads the reply from the text content blocks. The new test checks the request shape against a mocked transport. Three things go beyond the forced change or aren't proven by the check: the benchmark's model list is swapped, the SDK pin makes a major-version jump inside a tightly pinned requirements file, and the test imports `httpx2`, which isn't declared anywhere. The `verified` grade rests on one mocked test, so it proves the request shape but not live model IDs or that the dependencies install together.

concerns.issue: Line 12 changes `CLAUDE_MODEL` from `["claude-instant-1.2", "claude-2.0"]` to `["claude-haiku-4-5", "claude-sonnet-4-5"]`. Because of the `assert model_name in CLAUDE_MODEL` on line 26, any script, config or CLI argument that still passes the old names will now fail the assert. The swap also quietly changes which models the KoBBQ benchmark evaluates, so results are no longer comparable with earlier runs. The old models are likely retired, so a swap may be needed, but it is a product decision beyond the deprecation and should be called out. I could not confirm the new IDs against a live API; check Anthropic's models list.

`anthropic==0.2.10` jumps to `anthropic==2.4.0`. I can't confirm 2.4.0 from memory; check PyPI or the SDK changelog. A jump this large inside a fully pinned file risks resolver conflicts with `pydantic==2.5.2`, `pydantic_core==2.14.5`, `anyio==3.7.1`, `typing_extensions==4.12.2` and `openai==1.35.3`, and the new SDK may need a newer Python than the repo's environment (numpy 1.24.4 and torch 2.4.1 suggest Python 3.8–3.11). Nothing shows the full requirements.txt installs cleanly.

The test does `import httpx2 as httpx`, but `httpx2` is not in requirements.txt. It passes only if the CI environment pulls it in some other way, possibly transitively via the new SDK. I could not confirm that the SDK accepts an `httpx2.Client` as `http_client`; check the SDK's `_base_client` types. If it's a typo for `httpx`, the test is fragile.

The only check stubs out torch, requests, openai, transformers and tqdm and uses a MockTransport. It proves the request body and response parsing, but not a real API call, that the new model IDs are accepted, or that the real module imports with the pinned dependencies.

The output format changes slightly. The old completion text usually began with a leading space after `AI_PROMPT`, and the `HUMAN_PROMPT` stop sequence is gone. Any downstream KoBBQ answer parsing that depended on the old formatting could behave differently. The new form is probably cleaner, but worth a glance at the parsers.

checkFirst: Grep the repo (benchmark/kobbq scripts, configs, shell scripts, READMEs) for `claude-instant-1.2` and `claude-2.0`; those callers would now hit the assert on line 26.
Confirm `anthropic==2.4.0` exists and that `pip install -r requirements.txt` resolves alongside pydantic 2.5.2, anyio 3.7.1 and openai 1.35.3 on the repo's Python version.
Find where `httpx2` comes from and whether the SDK accepts its Client as `http_client`, or change the import to `httpx`.
Decide with the maintainers whether replacing the benchmarked Claude models is acceptable, and run one live call to confirm the new model IDs.
